owner: CC (code+proofs); Akien (the ordering ruling 2026-07-28: 'packet-inspector first' — and ratification of the filter admission, per the standing gate-filter rule)
intention: THE WIRE: the build_inspector gains PACKET JURISDICTION — a build is judged against the packet that charted it. Two small pieces of physics: (1) a packet may CLAIM ITS TICKET (optional 'ticket' field, gated: the claim must name a ticket on file in CairnCommons/tickets/ — a packet claiming an unfiled ticket is fabricated attribution and refuses at the berth door); (2) the component's own history names its tickets (crossings already carry them), so at a journaled PROVEME exit the inspector can FIND the berthed packets that charted this build with no new side channel — and judge the build against them. First filter through the new jurisdiction: charted_refs_resolve — every ref the packet charted must still resolve at promotion (the world must not have drifted from the chart between berth and promotion). Unreadable berths are named loudly, never skipped.
why: Akien's ordering, 2026-07-28: 'packet-inspector first' — the wire is the jurisdiction the constrain filters (next ticket) install into; without it a packet filter has nothing to run over. The filter's seeding failure is dated and measured: 2026-07-24, 'done' reported while the files stood unmoved — the claim drifted from the world and no gate compared them. The packet is the claim; the promotion is the moment; this filter is the comparison. The linkage design (packet claims ticket / history names tickets) opens no new door: both records already exist, the wire only reads them.
traces_to: Law 3 — a build's conformance to its chart is measured at the gate, not narrated
Law 4 — the comparison runs at the emit chokepoint's standing gate; no discipline, no memory required
Law 5 — the packet, the voyage, and the build share an address chain (berth -> ticket -> history) the gate can walk
Law 7 — an unreadable berth is a named finding, never a silent skip; a ticket claim naming no filed ticket refuses loudly
Law 8 — a promotion whose charted refs no longer resolve is a hollow claim; the gate refuses it
state: code-seam@v1: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> LEARNME -> [PROVED]   (cursor at PROVED 2026-07-28, same day as the cast; 14+2 teeth sealed under netns; live fire: a real packet claiming this ticket was FOUND via history->ticket->berth at build_inspector's own promotion and judged clean — then the constrain stones rode the jurisdiction the same day, chart's promotion judged against both its charted berths)
gates: proof gate: new teeth in test_inspector.py (fire-and-stay-quiet on synthetic berths; unreadable named; healthy stays clean) + a ticket-claim tooth in test_chart_orient.py, all under the tester's netns seal; test_inspector_nexus's allowlist tooth updated deliberately (cairn.chart.orient joins inspector.py's allowlist — a tree-free module, so the verdict-path/tree separation holds transitively) and re-sealed. Live gate: this ticket's own promotion crossings pass through the gate carrying the new filter.
falsifier: RED on any of: a packet claiming a ticket not on file passing the berth door; the inspector reaching packets through anything but the history->ticket->berth walk (a side channel); charted_refs_resolve firing on a component with no charted packets (a gate that always fires gets unwired); an unreadable berth silently skipped; cairn.chart.orient (or anything it imports) reaching tree machinery — the verdict path stays structurally tree-free; the existing 12 fire-path teeth or the chokepoint's gate teeth disturbed.
horizon: re-read when constrain-filters installs into this jurisdiction (the dependent ticket); when a later stage emits success_criteria (the filter this wire was named for grows then — v0 judges what packets already carry: refs); when packets berth for non-chart devices (the berth root generalizes).
distinctions_recorded: THE WIRE IS A JURISDICTION, NOT JUST A FILTER: the deliverable is the inspector's ability to find and judge charted packets; charted_refs_resolve is the first tenant, chosen because its seeding failure (2026-07-24) is the oldest sharpest instance of claim-vs-world drift.
NO NEW SIDE CHANNEL: packet claims ticket, history names tickets — both records pre-exist; the wire reads, it does not add a channel the gate must trust.

success_criteria WAITS HONESTLY: no stage emits them yet, so the v0 filter judges the strongest claim packets already make (refs). Building the criteria filter before the criteria exist would be a speculative contract — the constrain-filters ticket handles the one case where test-first is grounded (measured failures precede the module).
